It is false when it is mainly about things, places, stocks and the steps of a process (a kitchen, a supply chain, a garden, a factory), even if workers do those steps. Give a one-sentence why."}, {"role": "user", "content": "A partnership of four countries and a regional health network must decide by a deadline whether to activate a cross-border bio-surveillance early-warning system. Technical, legal, logistics and community groups each raise small, true but local concerns through their own channels to different members. Members meet regularly; the concerns slow meetings, reopen settled issues and make support conditional, which can delay or block deployment."}]

messages: [{"role": "system", "content": "Define a simulation world from the scenario using the schema. Every named actor has its own profile and memory. Profiles contain that actor's beliefs, not omniscient truth or required reactions. Claims may be false or disputed; information_items preserve the holder, intended recipients, apparent source, common source_lineage and hidden provenance. Separate actual technical state from claims, delivery, personal interpretation, public stance, recorded assent and institutional holds. Write public_summary using only facts explicitly shared by all actors before any delivery; never copy the omniscient description. World records declare visible_to_actor_ids for public_state; hidden_state stays private. Use stable neutral labels without private facts. Each actor's memories and profile contain only their declared knowledge, own interpretations and plausible personal tendencies. Do not copy narrator statements of withheld information into an actor's profile: 'Bo has not received the failure report' would itself tell Bo a failure report exists, and 'Mara was not given channel C or batch V17 detail' would reveal C and V17. Omit such narrator-only negatives entirely; do not replace them with invented beliefs. Personality, goals, ordinary preferences and explicitly held beliefs remain actor-facing, whether or not those beliefs are true. For information already received at the start use initially_delivered=true, holder_id as the receiving holder, recipient_ids including the holder, and source_id as the actual source person only when the source names one; otherwise leave source_id null rather than inventing a sender. Knowing a fact or holding detailed evidence does not establish that the person sent someone else's initial report. Preserve unspecified initial transmitter identity explicitly. Apparent source is a reported attribution, not proof of actual origin. A pending item defaults to initially_delivered=false and must not appear in an intended recipient's brief or memories. Canonical source_lineage may contain private origin details. Leave lineage_visible_to_actor_ids empty unless the source explicitly authorizes someone to know that common-origin identity. Seeing a report does not itself expose its hidden lineage. Use independent_decision for fresh collective activation/approval scenarios involving technical validation: declare required_actor_ids, validator_ids, repairer_ids, condition_initially_passing and initial_validation. This compiles actor-owned public stance and assent, requests for review, authorized repair and actual validation, a public technical hold and activation checks. A failed validation creates the hold; authorized passing revalidation clears only that hold. Repair is a declared effective technical intervention, never the passing of time. Reports never alter the technical condition or force agreement or assent. Use legacy decision only for explicitly stipulated scripted conditional-support fixtures, not as a model of persuasion. Do not duplicate compiled decision, condition, stance or assent records as world_records, even under semantic aliases. The compiled technical_condition owns current actual condition; keep only additional nonduplicated facts in world_records. Dated historical measurements and immutable reports may retain past failures after repair; label them as past evidence rather than assertions about the current actual condition. Regular meetings/deadlines may be scheduled_moments. Behaviors state possibilities, never prescribed actor responses. Use lowercase underscore ids. List omitted unsupported details and invented fidelity assumptions explicitly. No ending, social reaction, timer cure or recurrent conflict is required. Actors may disagree, ignore evidence or retain support."}, {"role": "user", "content": "A partnership of four countries and a regional health network must decide by a deadline whether to activate a cross-border bio-surveillance early-warning system. Technical, legal, logistics and community groups each raise small, true but local concerns through their own channels to different members. Members meet regularly; the concerns slow meetings, reopen settled issues and make support conditional, which can delay or block deployment."}]

Claims may be false or disputed; information_items preserve the holder, intended recipients, apparent source, common source_lineage and hidden provenance. Separate actual technical state from claims, delivery, personal interpretation, public stance, recorded assent and institutional holds. Write public_summary using only facts explicitly shared by all actors before any delivery; never copy the omniscient description. World records declare visible_to_actor_ids for public_state; hidden_state stays private. Use stable neutral labels without private facts. Each actor's memories and profile contain only their declared knowledge, own interpretations and plausible personal tendencies. Do not copy narrator statements of withheld information into an actor's profile: 'Bo has not received the failure report' would itself tell Bo a failure report exists, and 'Mara was not given channel C or batch V17 detail' would reveal C and V17. Omit such narrator-only negatives entirely; do not replace them with invented beliefs. Personality, goals, ordinary preferences and explicitly held beliefs remain actor-facing, whether or not those beliefs are true. For information already received at the start use initially_delivered=true, holder_id as the receiving holder, recipient_ids including the holder, and source_id as the actual source person only when the source names one; otherwise leave source_id null rather than inventing a sender. Knowing a fact or holding detailed evidence does not establish that the person sent someone else's initial report. Preserve unspecified initial transmitter identity explicitly. Apparent source is a reported attribution, not proof of actual origin. A pending item defaults to initially_delivered=false and must not appear in an intended recipient's brief or memories. Canonical source_lineage may contain private origin details. Leave lineage_visible_to_actor_ids empty unless the source explicitly authorizes someone to know that common-origin identity. Seeing a report does not itself expose its hidden lineage. Use independent_decision for fresh collective activation/approval scenarios involving technical validation: declare required_actor_ids, validator_ids, repairer_ids, condition_initially_passing and initial_validation. This compiles actor-owned public stance and assent, requests for review, authorized repair and actual validation, a public technical hold and activation checks. Reports never alter the technical condition or force agreement or assent. Use legacy decision only for explicitly stipulated scripted conditional-support fixtures, not as a model of persuasion. Do not duplicate compiled decision, condition, stance or assent records as world_records, even under semantic aliases. The compiled technical_condition owns current actual condition; keep only additional nonduplicated facts in world_records. Dated historical measurements and immutable reports may retain past failures after repair; label them as past evidence rather than assertions about the current actual condition. Regular meetings/deadlines may be scheduled_moments. Behaviors state possibilities, never prescribed actor responses. Use lowercase underscore ids.
